questions.prompt: Prove that m∠A + m∠B + m∠C = 180° in triangle ABC. Draw the line through C parallel to AB.
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that m∠A + m∠B + m∠C = 180° in triangle ABC. Draw the line through C parallel to AB.
questions.required_method: Name the two new angles at C, use alternate interior angles with AB, and the straight angle at C.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: (1) through C there is exactly one line parallel to AB (parallel postulate); (2) the angles it makes with CA and CB are congruent to ∠A and ∠B (alternate interior angles, transversals CA and CB); (3) those two angles and ∠ACB form a straight angle, 180°; (4) substitute. Invalid: measuring angles; citing the exterior angle theorem (it depends on this result).

questions.prompt: A proof of the triangle angle sum (line ℓ through C parallel to AB, making ∠1 next to CA and ∠2 next to CB): 1. m∠1 + m∠ACB + m∠2 = 180°  (?) 2. ∠1 ≅ ∠A and ∠2 ≅ ∠B  (?) 3. m∠A + m∠ACB + m∠B = 180°  (?) Give the three reasons.
questions.prompt_markup:
A proof of the triangle angle sum (line ℓ through C parallel to AB, making ∠1 next to CA and ∠2 next to CB):
1. m∠1 + m∠ACB + m∠2 = 180°  (?)
2. ∠1 ≅ ∠A and ∠2 ≅ ∠B  (?)
3. m∠A + m∠ACB + m∠B = 180°  (?)
Give the three reasons.
questions.correct_answer: 1: the angles form a straight angle (angle addition); 2: alternate interior angles are congruent (ℓ ∥ AB); 3: substitution.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent names for all three reasons.
